# 单篇讲义生成任务

项目仓库: llvm/llvm-project
项目名: llvm-project-lld
讲义目录: llvm-project-lld-tutorial/
代码永久链接 base: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/
当前 HEAD: 8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1
动作: new


---

## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论）

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。


## 完整大纲

```json
{
  "project": "llvm-project-lld",
  "rationale": "LLD 是 LLVM 子项目中体积庞大、性能极高的模块化链接器，单一可执行文件内同时包含 ELF、COFF、Mach-O、WebAssembly 四个近乎独立的链接后端。本手册以『从整体到局部、从主线到优化、以 ELF 为主线再横向对比其他后端』为编排原则：第一单元让读者建立项目定位、构建方式与多后端分发的整体认知；第二单元沿 ELF 的 link()→linkerMain→link<ELFT>→Writer 主线把链接全过程一次性走通；第三、四、五单元分别向下深入公共基础设施、输入与符号解析、输出布局与链接脚本三大支柱；第六、七单元进入重定位、目标架构、GC/ICF、LTO 等高阶机制；第八单元横向覆盖 COFF/Mach-O/wasm/MinGW 等其他后端；第九单元回到工程实践层面讲清测试体系、并行与性能剖析以及调试支持。每篇只解决一个相对独立的问题，依赖关系单向收敛，便于读者循序渐进。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "初识 LLD：定位、构建与多后端架构",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "项目概览与定位",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "介绍 LLD 是什么：LLVM 项目中替代系统链接器的高性能模块化链接器，支持 ELF/COFF/Mach-O/WebAssembly 四种目标格式，且可作为库嵌入。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解 LLD 在 LLVM 工具链中的定位与核心特性（快、可作为库、始终是交叉链接器）",
            "了解 LLD 支持的目标格式与 CPU/ABI 范围",
            "掌握阅读 LLD 源码时的主要参考文档与关键概念"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "docs/index.md",
            "docs/NewLLD.md"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "LLD 项目定位与特性",
            "支持的目标格式与后端",
            "NewLLD 设计文档的关键概念"
          ],
          "practice_task": "用 `clang -fuse-ld=lld` 链接一个 hello world 程序，用 `readelf --string-dump .comment` 确认输出由 LLD 产生；再对照 docs/index.md 列出 LLD 相对 GNU ld 的三条核心优势。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        },
        {
          "id": "u1-l2",
          "title": "构建与运行 LLD",
          "order": 2,
          "filename": "u1-l2-build-and-run.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "讲解如何用 CMake 构建 LLD、它的构建产物（ld.lld、lld-link 等），以及作为 LLVM 子项目或独立项目的两种构建方式。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "掌握 LLD 的 CMake 构建入口与关键选项（LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=lld、LLD_BUILD_TOOLS 等）",
            "理解独立构建与随 LLVM 构建两种模式的区别",
            "知道构建产物如何安装、如何替换系统默认链接器"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "CMakeLists.txt",
            "docs/index.md"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "CMakeLists 构建逻辑",
            "构建产物与符号链接",
            "lit 测试依赖（FileCheck/not/llvm-lit）"
          ],
          "practice_task": "克隆 llvm-project，用 `-DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=lld` 配置并构建出 ld.lld，再用 `-fuse-ld=lld` 验证可链接；记录 CMakeLists.txt 中 add_subdirectory 加入了哪些后端目录。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u1-l1"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        },
        {
          "id": "u1-l3",
          "title": "目录结构与多后端源码组织",
          "order": 3,
          "filename": "u1-l3-directory-structure.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "梳理 lld 仓库的目录结构：Common 公共基础设施、ELF/COFF/MachO/wasm 四个后端、tools/lld 分发器、include 公共头、test 与 unittests。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "掌握 lld 顶层目录的职责划分",
            "识别每个后端目录内重复出现的模块（Driver/SymbolTable/Symbols/Writer/ICF/MarkLive/LTO/MapFile）",
            "理解各后端『共享设计但很少共享代码』的原因"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "ELF/README.md",
            "COFF/README.md"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [

            "后端目录的共性模块",
            "test 与 unittests 的区别"
          ],
          "practice_task": "对照仓库结构，制作一张表格列出 ELF/COFF/MachO/wasm 各自的 Driver、SymbolTable、Writer、InputFiles 对应文件名；用一句话说明 Common 目录为何被四个后端共享。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u1-l1"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        },
        {
          "id": "u1-l4",
          "title": "单一可执行文件与 flavor 分发机制",
          "order": 4,
          "filename": "u1-l4-flavor-dispatch.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "讲解 LLD 单一可执行文件如何根据 argv[0]（ld.lld/lld-link/ld64.lld/wasm-ld）或 -flavor 选项分发到对应后端的 link() 函数。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解 tools/lld/lld.cpp 中 lld_main 的角色与 inTestVerbosity 的用途",
            "掌握 Flavor 枚举、getFlavor/parseProgname、isPETarget 的分发逻辑",
            "理解 LLD_ALL_DRIVERS / LLD_HAS_DRIVER 宏如何把后端 link 函数注册成分发表"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "tools/lld/lld.cpp",
            "include/lld/Common/Driver.h",
            "Common/DriverDispatcher.cpp"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [

            "DriverDispatcher 的 flavor 解析",
            "Driver.h 的注册宏与 Result"
          ],
          "practice_task": "为同一个 lld 可执行文件创建 ld.lld、lld-link、wasm-ld、ld64.lld 四个符号链接，分别运行 --version 观察分发到不同后端；再阅读 DriverDispatcher.cpp 写出 `lld -flavor gnu` 的解析过程。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u1-l3"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "u2",
      "title": "ELF 链接主线：从入口到写盘",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 2,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u2-l1",
          "title": "link() 入口与 Ctx 上下文对象",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u2-l1-elf-link-entry-and-ctx.md",
          "level": "intermediate",
          "topic": "讲解 ELF 后端的 link() 入口如何创建 Ctx 上下文（含 ErrorHandler、SymbolTable、LinkerScript）并交给 LinkerDriver::linkerMain 驱动整个链接。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解 elf::link() 的参数（args/stdout/stderr/exitEarly/disableOutput）与返回值含义",
            "掌握 Ctx（Config.h）作为 ELF 全局上下文聚合了哪些核心成员（symtab/script/driver/objectFiles 等）",
            "了解 ELFSyncStream（Err/Warn/Fatal/Msg）如何转发到 ErrorHandler"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "ELF/Driver.cpp",
            "ELF/Config.h",
            "include/lld/Common/CommonLinkerContext.h"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "elf::link() 入口",
            "Ctx 上下文聚合",
            "诊断流 ELFSyncStream"
          ],
          "practice_task": "在 elf::link() 中按顺序列出它创建的对象（Ctx、ErrorHandler、LinkerScript、symAux、SymbolTable），并解释为什么这些对象必须先于 linkerMain 存在。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u1-l4"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        },
        {
          "id": "u2-l2",
          "title": "linkerMain：选项解析、配置与文件加载",
          "order": 2,
          "filename": "u2-l2-linkermain-options-and-files.md",
          "level": "intermediate",
          "topic": "讲解 LinkerDriver::linkerMain 如何用 ELFOptTable 解析命令行、读取配置（readConfigs/setConfigs）、批量创建并并行加载输入文件（createFiles/loadFiles/addFile）。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解 linkerMain 的整体阶段：parse→readConfigs→createFiles→inferMachineType→setConfigs→checkOptions→link",
            "掌握 Options.td 与 ELFOptTable 如何声明和解析命令行选项",
            "理解 LoadJob 与 addFile 如何把不同文件类型（archive/obj/bitcode/shared）分类记录、再由 loadFiles 并行展开"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "ELF/Driver.cpp",
            "ELF/Driver.h",
            "ELF/Options.td"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "选项解析与配置读取",
            "createFiles/addFile 的 LoadJob 分类",
            "loadFiles 的并行文件加载"
          ],
          "practice_task": "用 `ld.lld --help` 导出选项列表，到 ELF/Options.td 中找到其中三个选项的定义；再在 addFile 中梳理 file_magic 的分支如何决定 LoadJob::Kind。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u2-l1"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        },
        {
          "id": "u2-l3",
          "title": "link<ELFT> 核心流水线全景",
          "order": 3,
          "filename": "u2-l3-link-template-pipeline.md",
          "level": "intermediate",
          "topic": "讲解 link<ELFT> 模板如何串联符号解析→LTO→段聚合→GC/ICF→调用 writeResult 的完整流水线，这是理解 LLD 的核心地图。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "掌握 link<ELFT> 中 parseFiles、compileBitcodeFiles、aggregate sections、markLive、createSyntheticSections、processSectionCommands、ICF、writeResult 的顺序与职责",
            "理解『惰性求值』设计：尽量推迟到必须时才读取 section 内容/重定位",
            "能定位流水线中每一步对应的源码位置与 TimeTraceScope 标注"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "ELF/Driver.cpp"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [

            "u2-l2"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        },

          "id": "u2-l4",
          "title": "Writer 的写盘阶段",
          "order": 4,
          "filename": "u2-l4-writer-run-phases.md",
          "level": "intermediate",
          "topic": "讲解 Writer<ELFT>::run() 如何完成段内容定稿、地址/文件偏移分配、程序头生成，以及最终把 ELF 头和各段写到 mmap 输出文件。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解 Writer::run 的阶段：finalizeSections→maybeCompress→assignFileOffsets→setPhdrs→writeHeader/writeSections→writeBuildId",
            "掌握 finalizeSections 与 assignAddresses 为何需要多次迭代（地址相关内容相互依赖）",
            "理解 openFile/commit 与 -o -（写到 stdout）的特殊处理"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "ELF/Writer.cpp",
            "ELF/Writer.h"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "finalizeSections 与迭代定稿",
            "assignFileOffsets/setPhdrs",
            "writeHeader/writeSections/writeBuildId 与输出提交"
          ],
          "practice_task": "在 Writer::run() 中标注每一步会改变输出大小的操作（如 maybeCompress），并解释为什么 writeBuildId 必须放在最后。",
          "depends_on": [
            "u2-l3"
          ],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "u3",
      "title": "公共基础设施 Common",
      "level": "intermediate",
      "order": 3,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u3-l1",
          "title": "CommonLinkerContext 与全局状态聚合",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u3-l1-common-linker-context.md",
          "level": "intermediate",
          "topic": "讲解 CommonLinkerContext 如何把 LLD 的全局状态（BumpPtrAllocator、StringSaver、ErrorHandler）聚合到堆对象上，从而支持把 LLD 作为库安全地反复调用。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "理解为什么 LLD 不用程序级全局变量而用 CommonLinkerContext 聚合",
            "掌握 bAlloc/saver/uniqueSaver 与 context<T>() 访问方式",
            "了解 SpecificAllocBase instances 表的作用"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "include/lld/Common/CommonLinkerContext.h",
            "Common/CommonLinkerContext.cpp",
            "ELF/Config.h"

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览与定位

本讲是 LLD 学习手册的开篇，只读文档与顶层目录以建立全局地图，含三个最小模块。其一，定位：LLD 是 LLVM 项目的高性能模块化链接器，旨在直接替换 GNU ld、link.exe、ld64 等系统链接器，核心特性是快、可作为库嵌入（lld::lldMain）、始终是交叉链接器。其二，格式与后端：同一个二进制内含四个链接器，分别处理 ELF、PE/COFF、Mach-O、WebAssembly，对应 ELF/、COFF/、MachO/、wasm/ 四个目录，外加公共层 Common/ 与分发器 tools/lld/；四个后端"共享设计、几乎不共享代码"，没有抽象公共层，故手册以 ELF 为主线讲解。其三，NewLLD 概念地图：三条设计原则为原生实现共享设计不共享代码、Speed by design（少做事胜过高效做事，体现为惰性求值）、高效静态库处理（记住全部符号、按需即时提取，使 --start-group 基本成为 no-op）；关键数据结构有 Symbol（分 Defined/Undefined/Lazy，用 placement new 就地替换使旧指针自动指向解析结果）、SymbolTable、InputSection（ELF）/Chunk（COFF）、OutputSection；三个角色为 InputFile、Driver、Writer，Driver 以六步（解析命令行→建符号表→建 InputFile→查未定义符号→建 Writer→写出结果）驱动全流程。若需确认输出是否由 LLD 链接，可查看输出 .comment 段中的 Linker: LLD 标记。
### u1-l2 构建与运行 LLD

本讲解决「LLD 源码如何变成可用链接器」，分三个模块。其一，LLD 作为 monorepo 子项目，有「随 LLVM 构建」（`-DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=lld`，最常用）与「独立构建」（`LLD_BUILT_STANDALONE`，自行 `find_package(LLVM)`）两种形态，靠比较 `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` 与 `CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR` 判定；顶层用 `add_subdirectory` 无条件纳入 Common 及 ELF/COFF/MachO/wasm 四后端，印证 LLD 始终是全架构交叉链接器。其二，构建只产出唯一可执行目标 `lld`，再经符号链接变出 `ld.lld`、`lld-link`、`ld64.lld`、`wasm-ld` 四个名字，运行时据 `argv[0]` 做 flavor 分发（下讲详述）；`LLD_BUILD_TOOLS` 控制是否编出可执行文件。其三，lit 测试（`check-lld`）重度依赖 FileCheck、llvm-readelf 等 LLVM 工具，借 `LLD_IN_TEST` 连跑两遍 main 验证可重入性。实际使用多以 `clang -fuse-ld=lld` 或符号链接覆盖 `/usr/bin/ld` 调用。

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览与定位

本讲是 LLD 学习手册的开篇，只读文档与顶层目录以建立全局地图，含三个最小模块。其一，定位：LLD 是 LLVM 项目的高性能模块化链接器，旨在直接替换 GNU ld、link.exe、ld64 等系统链接器，核心特性是快、可作为库嵌入（lld::lldMain）、始终是交叉链接器。其二，格式与后端：同一个二进制内含四个链接器，分别处理 ELF、PE/COFF、Mach-O、WebAssembly，对应 ELF/、COFF/、MachO/、wasm/ 四个目录，外加公共层 Common/ 与分发器 tools/lld/；四个后端"共享设计、几乎不共享代码"，没有抽象公共层，故手册以 ELF 为主线讲解。其三，NewLLD 概念地图：三条设计原则为原生实现共享设计不共享代码、Speed by design（少做事胜过高效做事，体现为惰性求值）、高效静态库处理（记住全部符号、按需即时提取，使 --start-group 基本成为 no-op）；关键数据结构有 Symbol（分 Defined/Undefined/Lazy，用 placement new 就地替换使旧指针自动指向解析结果）、SymbolTable、InputSection（ELF）/Chunk（COFF）、OutputSection；三个角色为 InputFile、Driver、Writer，Driver 以六步（解析命令行→建符号表→建 InputFile→查未定义符号→建 Writer→写出结果）驱动全流程。若需确认输出是否由 LLD 链接，可查看输出 .comment 段中的 Linker: LLD 标记。
### u1-l2 构建与运行 LLD

本讲解决「LLD 源码如何变成可用链接器」，分三个模块。其一，LLD 作为 monorepo 子项目，有「随 LLVM 构建」（`-DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=lld`，最常用）与「独立构建」（`LLD_BUILT_STANDALONE`，自行 `find_package(LLVM)`）两种形态，靠比较 `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` 与 `CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR` 判定；顶层用 `add_subdirectory` 无条件纳入 Common 及 ELF/COFF/MachO/wasm 四后端，印证 LLD 始终是全架构交叉链接器。其二，构建只产出唯一可执行目标 `lld`，再经符号链接变出 `ld.lld`、`lld-link`、`ld64.lld`、`wasm-ld` 四个名字，运行时据 `argv[0]` 做 flavor 分发（下讲详述）；`LLD_BUILD_TOOLS` 控制是否编出可执行文件。其三，lit 测试（`check-lld`）重度依赖 FileCheck、llvm-readelf 等 LLVM 工具，借 `LLD_IN_TEST` 连跑两遍 main 验证可重入性。实际使用多以 `clang -fuse-ld=lld` 或符号链接覆盖 `/usr/bin/ld` 调用。

content.content:
1	# The ELF, COFF and Wasm Linkers
2	
3	## The ELF Linker as a Library
4	
5	You can embed LLD to your program by linking against it and calling the linker's
6	entry point function `lld::lldMain`.
7	
8	The current policy is that it is your responsibility to give trustworthy object
9	files. The function is guaranteed to return as long as you do not pass corrupted
10	or malicious object files. A corrupted file could cause a fatal error or SEGV.
11	That being said, you don't need to worry too much about it if you create object
12	files in the usual way and give them to the linker. It is naturally expected to
13	work, or otherwise it's a linker's bug.
14	
15	# Design
16	
17	We will describe the design of the linkers in the rest of the document.
18	
19	## Key Concepts
20	
21	Linkers are fairly large pieces of software.
22	There are many design choices you have to make to create a complete linker.
23	
24	This is a list of design choices we've made for ELF and COFF LLD.
25	We believe that these high-level design choices achieved a right balance
26	between speed, simplicity and extensibility.
27	
28	- Implement as native linkers
29	
30	  We implemented the linkers as native linkers for each file format.
31	
32	  The linkers share the same design but share very little code.
33	  Sharing code makes sense if the benefit is worth its cost.
34	  In our case, the object formats are different enough that we thought the layer
35	  to abstract the differences wouldn't be worth its complexity and run-time
36	  cost. Elimination of the abstract layer has greatly simplified the
37	  implementation.
38	
39	- Speed by design
40	
41	  One of the most important things in achieving high performance is to
42	  do less rather than do it efficiently.
43	  Therefore, the high-level design matters more than local optimizations.
44	  Since we are trying to create a high-performance linker,
45	  it is very important to keep the design as efficient as possible.
46	
47	  Broadly speaking, we do not do anything until we have to do it.
48	  For example, we do not read section contents or relocations
49	  until we need them to continue linking.
50	  When we need to do some costly operation (such as looking up
51	  a hash table for each symbol), we do it only once.
52	  We obtain a handle (which is typically just a pointer to actual data)
53	  on the first operation and use it throughout the process.
54	
55	- Efficient archive file handling
56	
57	  LLD's handling of archive files (the files with ".a" file extension) is
58	  different from the traditional Unix linkers and similar to Windows linkers.
59	  We'll describe how the traditional Unix linker handles archive files, what the
60	  problem is, and how LLD approached the problem.
61	
62	  The traditional Unix linker maintains a set of undefined symbols during
63	  linking. The linker visits each file in the order as they appeared in the
64	  command line until the set becomes empty. What the linker would do depends on
65	  file type.
66	
67	  - If the linker visits an object file, the linker links object files to the
68	    result, and undefined symbols in the object file are added to the set.
69	  - If the linker visits an archive file, it checks for the archive file's
70	    symbol table and extracts all object files that have definitions for any
71	    symbols in the set.
72	
73	  This algorithm sometimes leads to a counter-intuitive behavior. If you give
74	  archive files before object files, nothing will happen because when the linker
75	  visits archives, there are no undefined symbols in the set. As a result, no
76	  files are extracted from the first archive file, and the link is done at that
77	  point because the set is empty after it visits one file.
78	
79	  You can fix the problem by reordering the files,
80	  but that cannot fix the issue of mutually-dependent archive files.
81	
82	  Linking mutually-dependent archive files is tricky. You may specify the same
83	  archive file multiple times to let the linker visit it more than once. Or,
84	  you may use the special command line options, `--start-group` and
85	  `--end-group`, to let the linker loop over the files between the options until
86	  no new symbols are added to the set.
87	
88	  Visiting the same archive files multiple times makes the linker slower.
89	
90	  Here is how LLD approaches the problem. Instead of memorizing only undefined
91	  symbols, we program LLD so that it memorizes all symbols. When it sees an
92	  undefined symbol that can be resolved by extracting an object file from an
93	  archive file it previously visited, it immediately extracts the file and links
94	  it. It is doable because LLD does not forget symbols it has seen in archive
95	  files.
96	
97	  We believe that LLD's way is efficient and easy to justify.
98	
99	  The semantics of LLD's archive handling are different from the traditional
100	  Unix's. You can observe it if you carefully craft archive files to exploit
101	  it. However, in reality, we don't know any program that cannot link with our
102	  algorithm so far, so it's not going to cause trouble.
103	
104	## Numbers You Want to Know
105	
106	To give you intuition about what kinds of data the linker is mainly working on,
107	I'll give you the list of objects and their numbers LLD has to read and process
108	in order to link a very large executable. In order to link Chrome with debug
109	info, which is roughly 2 GB in output size, LLD reads
110	
111	- 17,000 files,
112	- 1,800,000 sections,
113	- 6,300,000 symbols, and
114	- 13,000,000 relocations.
115	
116	LLD produces the 2 GB executable in 15 seconds.
117	
118	These numbers vary depending on your program, but in general,
119	you have a lot of relocations and symbols for each file.
120	If your program is written in C++, symbol names are likely to be
121	pretty long because of name mangling.
122	
123	It is important to not waste time on relocations and symbols.
124	
125	In the above case, the total amount of symbol strings is 450 MB,
126	and inserting all of them to a hash table takes 1.5 seconds.
127	Therefore, if you causally add a hash table lookup for each symbol,
128	it would slow down the linker by 10%. So, don't do that.
129	
130	On the other hand, you don't have to pursue efficiency
131	when handling files.
132	
133	## Important Data Structures
134	
135	We will describe the key data structures in LLD in this section. The linker can
136	be understood as the interactions between them. Once you understand their
137	functions, the code of the linker should look obvious to you.
138	
139	- Symbol
140	
141	  This class represents a symbol.
142	  They are created for symbols in object files or archive files.
143	  The linker creates linker-defined symbols as well.
144	
145	  There are basically three types of Symbols: Defined, Undefined, or Lazy.
146	
147	  - Defined symbols are for all symbols that are considered as "resolved",
148	    including real defined symbols, COMDAT symbols, common symbols,
149	    absolute symbols, linker-created symbols, etc.
150	  - Undefined symbols represent undefined symbols, which need to be replaced by
151	    Defined symbols by the resolver until the link is complete.
152	  - Lazy symbols represent symbols we found in archive file headers
153	    which can turn into Defined if we read archive members.
154	
155	  There's only one Symbol instance for each unique symbol name. This uniqueness
156	  is guaranteed by the symbol table. As the resolver reads symbols from input
157	  files, it replaces an existing Symbol with the "best" Symbol for its symbol
158	  name using the placement new.
159	
160	  The above mechanism allows you to use pointers to Symbols as a very cheap way
161	  to access name resolution results. Assume for example that you have a pointer
162	  to an undefined symbol before name resolution. If the symbol is resolved to a
163	  defined symbol by the resolver, the pointer will "automatically" point to the
164	  defined symbol, because the undefined symbol the pointer pointed to will have
165	  been replaced by the defined symbol in-place.
166	
167	- SymbolTable
168	
169	  SymbolTable is basically a hash table from strings to Symbols
170	  with logic to resolve symbol conflicts. It resolves conflicts by symbol type.
171	
172	  - If we add Defined and Undefined symbols, the symbol table will keep the
173	    former.
174	  - If we add Defined and Lazy symbols, it will keep the former.
175	  - If we add Lazy and Undefined, it will keep the former,
176	    but it will also trigger the Lazy symbol to load the archive member
177	    to actually resolve the symbol.
178	
179	- Chunk (COFF specific)
180	
181	  Chunk represents a chunk of data that will occupy space in an output.
182	  Each regular section becomes a chunk.
183	  Chunks created for common or BSS symbols are not backed by sections.
184	  The linker may create chunks to append additional data to an output as well.
185	
186	  Chunks know about their size, how to copy their data to mmap'ed outputs,
187	  and how to apply relocations to them.
188	  Specifically, section-based chunks know how to read relocation tables
189	  and how to apply them.
190	
191	- InputSection (ELF specific)
192	
193	  Since we have less synthesized data for ELF, we don't abstract slices of
194	  input files as Chunks for ELF. Instead, we directly use the input section
195	  as an internal data type.
196	
197	  InputSection knows about their size and how to copy themselves to
198	  mmap'ed outputs, just like COFF Chunks.
199	
200	- OutputSection
201	
202	  OutputSection is a container of InputSections (ELF) or Chunks (COFF).
203	  An InputSection or Chunk belongs to at most one OutputSection.
204	
205	There are mainly three actors in this linker.
206	
207	- InputFile
208	
209	  InputFile is a superclass of file readers.
210	  We have a different subclass for each input file type,
211	  such as regular object file, archive file, etc.
212	  They are responsible for creating and owning Symbols and InputSections/Chunks.
213	
214	- Writer
215	
216	  The writer is responsible for writing file headers and InputSections/Chunks to
217	  a file. It creates OutputSections, puts all InputSections/Chunks into them,
218	  assigns unique, non-overlapping addresses and file offsets to them, and then
219	  writes them down to a file.
220	
221	- Driver
222	
223	  The linking process is driven by the driver. The driver:
224	
225	  - processes command line options,
226	  - creates a symbol table,
227	  - creates an InputFile for each input file and puts all symbols within into
228	    the symbol table,
229	  - checks if there's no remaining undefined symbols,
230	  - creates a writer,
231	  - and passes the symbol table to the writer to write the result to a file.
232	
233	## Link-Time Optimization
234	
235	LTO is implemented by handling LLVM bitcode files as object files.
236	The linker resolves symbols in bitcode files normally. If all symbols
237	are successfully resolved, it then runs LLVM passes
238	with all bitcode files to convert them to one big regular ELF/COFF file.
239	Finally, the linker replaces bitcode symbols with ELF/COFF symbols,
240	so that they are linked as if they were in the native format from the beginning.
241	
242	The details are described in this document.
243	<https://llvm.org/docs/LinkTimeOptimization.html>

247	- RVA (COFF)
248	
249	  Short for Relative Virtual Address.
250	
251	  Windows executables or DLLs are not position-independent; they are
252	  linked against a fixed address called an image base. RVAs are
253	  offsets from an image base.
254	
255	  Default image bases are 0x140000000 for executables and 0x18000000
256	  for DLLs. For example, when we are creating an executable, we assume
257	  that the executable will be loaded at address 0x140000000 by the
258	  loader, so we apply relocations accordingly. Result texts and data
259	  will contain raw absolute addresses.
260	
261	- VA
262	
263	  Short for Virtual Address. For COFF, it is equivalent to RVA + image base.
264	
265	- Base relocations (COFF)
266	
267	  Relocation information for the loader. If the loader decides to map
268	  an executable or a DLL to a different address than their image
269	  bases, it fixes up binaries using information contained in the base
270	  relocation table. A base relocation table consists of a list of
271	  locations containing addresses. The loader adds a difference between
272	  RVA and actual load address to all locations listed there.
273	
274	  Note that this run-time relocation mechanism is much simpler than ELF.
275	  There's no PLT or GOT. Images are relocated as a whole just
276	  by shifting entire images in memory by some offsets. Although doing
277	  this breaks text sharing, I think this mechanism is not actually bad
278	  on today's computers.
279	
280	- ICF
281	
282	  Short for Identical COMDAT Folding (COFF) or Identical Code Folding (ELF).
283	
284	  ICF is an optimization to reduce output size by merging read-only sections
285	  by not only their names but by their contents. If two read-only sections
286	  happen to have the same metadata, actual contents and relocations,
287	  they are merged by ICF. It is known as an effective technique,
288	  and it usually reduces C++ program's size by a few percent or more.
289	
290	  Note that this is not an entirely sound optimization. C/C++ require
291	  different functions to have different addresses. If a program depends on
292	  that property, it would fail at runtime.
293	
294	  On Windows, that's not really an issue because MSVC link.exe enabled
295	  the optimization by default. As long as your program works
296	  with the linker's default settings, your program should be safe with ICF.
297	
298	  On Unix, your program is generally not guaranteed to be safe with ICF,
299	  although large programs happen to work correctly.
300	  LLD works fine with ICF for example.

# The ELF, COFF and Wasm Linkers

## The ELF Linker as a Library

You can embed LLD to your program by linking against it and calling the linker's
entry point function `lld::lldMain`.

The current policy is that it is your responsibility to give trustworthy object
files. The function is guaranteed to return as long as you do not pass corrupted
or malicious object files. A corrupted file could cause a fatal error or SEGV.
That being said, you don't need to worry too much about it if you create object
files in the usual way and give them to the linker. It is naturally expected to
work, or otherwise it's a linker's bug.

# Design

We will describe the design of the linkers in the rest of the document.

## Key Concepts

Linkers are fairly large pieces of software.
There are many design choices you have to make to create a complete linker.

This is a list of design choices we've made for ELF and COFF LLD.
We believe that these high-level design choices achieved a right balance
between speed, simplicity and extensibility.

- Implement as native linkers

  We implemented the linkers as native linkers for each file format.

  The linkers share the same design but share very little code.
  Sharing code makes sense if the benefit is worth its cost.
  In our case, the object formats are different enough that we thought the layer
  to abstract the differences wouldn't be worth its complexity and run-time
  cost. Elimination of the abstract layer has greatly simplified the
  implementation.

- Speed by design

  One of the most important things in achieving high performance is to
  do less rather than do it efficiently.
  Therefore, the high-level design matters more than local optimizations.
  Since we are trying to create a high-performance linker,
  it is very important to keep the design as efficient as possible.

  Broadly speaking, we do not do anything until we have to do it.
  For example, we do not read section contents or relocations
  until we need them to continue linking.
  When we need to do some costly operation (such as looking up
  a hash table for each symbol), we do it only once.
  We obtain a handle (which is typically just a pointer to actual data)
  on the first operation and use it throughout the process.

- Efficient archive file handling

  LLD's handling of archive files (the files with ".a" file extension) is
  different from the traditional Unix linkers and similar to Windows linkers.
  We'll describe how the traditional Unix linker handles archive files, what the
  problem is, and how LLD approached the problem.

  The traditional Unix linker maintains a set of undefined symbols during
  linking. The linker visits each file in the order as they appeared in the
  command line until the set becomes empty. What the linker would do depends on
  file type.

  - If the linker visits an object file, the linker links object files to the
    result, and undefined symbols in the object file are added to the set.
  - If the linker visits an archive file, it checks for the archive file's
    symbol table and extracts all object files that have definitions for any
    symbols in the set.

  This algorithm sometimes leads to a counter-intuitive behavior. If you give
  archive files before object files, nothing will happen because when the linker
  visits archives, there are no undefined symbols in the set. As a result, no
  files are extracted from the first archive file, and the link is done at that
  point because the set is empty after it visits one file.

  You can fix the problem by reordering the files,
  but that cannot fix the issue of mutually-dependent archive files.

  Linking mutually-dependent archive files is tricky. You may specify the same
  archive file multiple times to let the linker visit it more than once. Or,
  you may use the special command line options, `--start-group` and
  `--end-group`, to let the linker loop over the files between the options until
  no new symbols are added to the set.

  Visiting the same archive files multiple times makes the linker slower.

  Here is how LLD approaches the problem. Instead of memorizing only undefined
  symbols, we program LLD so that it memorizes all symbols. When it sees an
  undefined symbol that can be resolved by extracting an object file from an
  archive file it previously visited, it immediately extracts the file and links
  it. It is doable because LLD does not forget symbols it has seen in archive
  files.

  We believe that LLD's way is efficient and easy to justify.

  The semantics of LLD's archive handling are different from the traditional
  Unix's. You can observe it if you carefully craft archive files to exploit
  it. However, in reality, we don't know any program that cannot link with our
  algorithm so far, so it's not going to cause trouble.

## Numbers You Want to Know

To give you intuition about what kinds of data the linker is mainly working on,
I'll give you the list of objects and their numbers LLD has to read and process
in order to link a very large executable. In order to link Chrome with debug
info, which is roughly 2 GB in output size, LLD reads

- 17,000 files,
- 1,800,000 sections,
- 6,300,000 symbols, and
- 13,000,000 relocations.

LLD produces the 2 GB executable in 15 seconds.

These numbers vary depending on your program, but in general,
you have a lot of relocations and symbols for each file.
If your program is written in C++, symbol names are likely to be
pretty long because of name mangling.

It is important to not waste time on relocations and symbols.

In the above case, the total amount of symbol strings is 450 MB,
and inserting all of them to a hash table takes 1.5 seconds.
Therefore, if you causally add a hash table lookup for each symbol,
it would slow down the linker by 10%. So, don't do that.

On the other hand, you don't have to pursue efficiency
when handling files.

## Important Data Structures

We will describe the key data structures in LLD in this section. The linker can
be understood as the interactions between them. Once you understand their
functions, the code of the linker should look obvious to you.

- Symbol

  This class represents a symbol.
  They are created for symbols in object files or archive files.
  The linker creates linker-defined symbols as well.

  There are basically three types of Symbols: Defined, Undefined, or Lazy.

  - Defined symbols are for all symbols that are considered as "resolved",
    including real defined symbols, COMDAT symbols, common symbols,
    absolute symbols, linker-created symbols, etc.
  - Undefined symbols represent undefined symbols, which need to be replaced by
    Defined symbols by the resolver until the link is complete.
  - Lazy symbols represent symbols we found in archive file headers
    which can turn into Defined if we read archive members.

  There's only one Symbol instance for each unique symbol name. This uniqueness
  is guaranteed by the symbol table. As the resolver reads symbols from input
  files, it replaces an existing Symbol with the "best" Symbol for its symbol
  name using the placement new.

  The above mechanism allows you to use pointers to Symbols as a very cheap way
  to access name resolution results. Assume for example that you have a pointer
  to an undefined symbol before name resolution. If the symbol is resolved to a
  defined symbol by the resolver, the pointer will "automatically" point to the
  defined symbol, because the undefined symbol the pointer pointed to will have
  been replaced by the defined symbol in-place.

- SymbolTable

  SymbolTable is basically a hash table from strings to Symbols
  with logic to resolve symbol conflicts. It resolves conflicts by symbol type.

  - If we add Defined and Undefined symbols, the symbol table will keep the
    former.
  - If we add Defined and Lazy symbols, it will keep the former.
  - If we add Lazy and Undefined, it will keep the former,
    but it will also trigger the Lazy symbol to load the archive member
    to actually resolve the symbol.

- Chunk (COFF specific)

  Chunk represents a chunk of data that will occupy space in an output.
  Each regular section becomes a chunk.
  Chunks created for common or BSS symbols are not backed by sections.
  The linker may create chunks to append additional data to an output as well.

  Chunks know about their size, how to copy their data to mmap'ed outputs,
  and how to apply relocations to them.
  Specifically, section-based chunks know how to read relocation tables
  and how to apply them.

- InputSection (ELF specific)

  Since we have less synthesized data for ELF, we don't abstract slices of
  input files as Chunks for ELF. Instead, we directly use the input section
  as an internal data type.

  InputSection knows about their size and how to copy themselves to
  mmap'ed outputs, just like COFF Chunks.

- OutputSection

  OutputSection is a container of InputSections (ELF) or Chunks (COFF).
  An InputSection or Chunk belongs to at most one OutputSection.

There are mainly three actors in this linker.

- InputFile

  InputFile is a superclass of file readers.
  We have a different subclass for each input file type,
  such as regular object file, archive file, etc.
  They are responsible for creating and owning Symbols and InputSections/Chunks.

- Writer

  The writer is responsible for writing file headers and InputSections/Chunks to
  a file. It creates OutputSections, puts all InputSections/Chunks into them,
  assigns unique, non-overlapping addresses and file offsets to them, and then
  writes them down to a file.

- Driver

  The linking process is driven by the driver. The driver:

  - processes command line options,
  - creates a symbol table,
  - creates an InputFile for each input file and puts all symbols within into
    the symbol table,
  - checks if there's no remaining undefined symbols,
  - creates a writer,
  - and passes the symbol table to the writer to write the result to a file.

## Link-Time Optimization

LTO is implemented by handling LLVM bitcode files as object files.
The linker resolves symbols in bitcode files normally. If all symbols
are successfully resolved, it then runs LLVM passes
with all bitcode files to convert them to one big regular ELF/COFF file.
Finally, the linker replaces bitcode symbols with ELF/COFF symbols,
so that they are linked as if they were in the native format from the beginning.

The details are described in this document.
<https://llvm.org/docs/LinkTimeOptimization.html>

## Glossary

- RVA (COFF)

  Short for Relative Virtual Address.

  Windows executables or DLLs are not position-independent; they are
  linked against a fixed address called an image base. RVAs are
  offsets from an image base.

  Default image bases are 0x140000000 for executables and 0x18000000
  for DLLs. For example, when we are creating an executable, we assume
  that the executable will be loaded at address 0x140000000 by the
  loader, so we apply relocations accordingly. Result texts and data
  will contain raw absolute addresses.

- VA

  Short for Virtual Address. For COFF, it is equivalent to RVA + image base.

- Base relocations (COFF)

  Relocation information for the loader. If the loader decides to map
  an executable or a DLL to a different address than their image
  bases, it fixes up binaries using information contained in the base
  relocation table. A base relocation table consists of a list of
  locations containing addresses. The loader adds a difference between
  RVA and actual load address to all locations listed there.

  Note that this run-time relocation mechanism is much simpler than ELF.
  There's no PLT or GOT. Images are relocated as a whole just
  by shifting entire images in memory by some offsets. Although doing
  this breaks text sharing, I think this mechanism is not actually bad
  on today's computers.

- ICF

  Short for Identical COMDAT Folding (COFF) or Identical Code Folding (ELF).

  ICF is an optimization to reduce output size by merging read-only sections
  by not only their names but by their contents. If two read-only sections
  happen to have the same metadata, actual contents and relocations,
  they are merged by ICF. It is known as an effective technique,
  and it usually reduces C++ program's size by a few percent or more.

  Note that this is not an entirely sound optimization. C/C++ require
  different functions to have different addresses. If a program depends on
  that property, it would fail at runtime.

  On Windows, that's not really an issue because MSVC link.exe enabled
  the optimization by default. As long as your program works
  with the linker's default settings, your program should be safe with ICF.

  On Unix, your program is generally not guaranteed to be safe with ICF,
  although large programs happen to work correctly.
  LLD works fine with ICF for example.

## Other Info

:maxdepth: 1

```

# LLD - The LLVM Linker

LLD is a linker from the LLVM project that is a drop-in replacement
for system linkers and runs much faster than them. It also provides
features that are useful for toolchain developers.

The linker supports ELF (Unix), PE/COFF (Windows), Mach-O (macOS) and
WebAssembly in descending order of completeness. Internally, LLD consists of
several different linkers. The ELF port is the one that will be described in
this document. The PE/COFF port is complete, including
Windows debug info (PDB) support.

## Features

- LLD is a drop-in replacement for the GNU linkers that accepts the
  same command line arguments and linker scripts as GNU.
- LLD is very fast. When you link a large program on a multicore
  machine, you can expect that LLD runs more than twice as fast as the GNU
  gold linker. Your mileage may vary, though.
- It supports various CPUs/ABIs including AArch64, AMDGPU, ARM, Hexagon,
  LoongArch, MIPS 32/64 big/little-endian, PowerPC, PowerPC64, RISC-V,
  SPARC V9, x86-32 and x86-64. Among these, AArch64, ARM (>= v4), LoongArch,
  PowerPC, PowerPC64, RISC-V, x86-32 and x86-64 have production quality.
  MIPS seems decent too.
- It is always a cross-linker, meaning that it always supports all the
  above targets however it was built. In fact, we don't provide a
  build-time option to enable/disable each target. This should make it
  easy to use our linker as part of a cross-compile toolchain.
- You can embed LLD in your program to eliminate dependencies on
  external linkers. All you have to do is to construct object files
  and command line arguments just like you would do to invoke an
  external linker and then call the linker's main function,
  `lld::lldMain`, from your code.
- It is small. We are using LLVM libObject library to read from object
  files, so it is not a completely fair comparison, but as of February
  2017, LLD/ELF consists only of 21k lines of C++ code while GNU gold
  consists of 198k lines of C++ code.
- Link-time optimization (LTO) is supported by default. Essentially,
  all you have to do to do LTO is to pass the `-flto` option to clang.
  Then clang creates object files not in the native object file format
  but in LLVM bitcode format. LLD reads bitcode object files, compile
  them using LLVM and emit an output file. Because in this way LLD can
  see the entire program, it can do the whole program optimization.
- Some very old features for ancient Unix systems (pre-90s or even
  before that) have been removed. Some default settings have been
  tuned for the 21st century. For example, the stack is marked as
  non-executable by default to tighten security.

## Performance

This is a link time comparison on a 2-socket 20-core 40-thread Xeon
E5-2680 2.80 GHz machine with an SSD drive. We ran gold and lld with
or without multi-threading support. To disable multi-threading, we
added `-no-threads` to the command lines.

| Program | Output size | GNU ld | GNU gold w/o threads | GNU gold w/threads | lld w/o threads | lld w/threads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ffmpeg dbg | 92 MiB | 1.72s | 1.16s | 1.01s | 0.60s | 0.35s |
| mysqld dbg | 154 MiB | 8.50s | 2.96s | 2.68s | 1.06s | 0.68s |
| clang dbg | 1.67 GiB | 104.03s | 34.18s | 23.49s | 14.82s | 5.28s |
| chromium dbg | 1.14 GiB | 209.05s[^1] | 64.70s | 60.82s | 27.60s | 16.70s |

As you can see, lld is significantly faster than GNU linkers.
Note that this is just a benchmark result of our environment.
Depending on number of available cores, available amount of memory or
disk latency/throughput, your results may vary.

[^1]: Since GNU ld doesn't support the `-icf=all` and
    `-gdb-index` options, we removed them from the command line
    for GNU ld. GNU ld would have been slower than this if it had
    these options.

## Build

If you have already checked out LLVM using SVN, you can check out LLD
under `tools` directory just like you probably did for clang. For the
details, see [Getting Started with the LLVM System](https://llvm.org/docs/GettingStarted.html).

If you haven't checked out LLVM, the easiest way to build LLD is to
check out the entire LLVM projects/sub-projects from a git mirror and
build that tree. You need `cmake` and of course a C++ compiler.

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project llvm-project
$ mkdir build
$ cd build
$ cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=lld -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local ../llvm-project/llvm
$ make install
```

## Using LLD

LLD is installed as `ld.lld`. On Unix, linkers are invoked by
compiler drivers, so you are not expected to use that command
directly. There are a few ways to tell compiler drivers to use ld.lld
instead of the default linker.

The easiest way to do that is to overwrite the default linker. After
installing LLD to somewhere on your disk, you can create a symbolic
link by doing `ln -s /path/to/ld.lld /usr/bin/ld` so that
`/usr/bin/ld` is resolved to LLD.

If you don't want to change the system setting, you can use clang's
`-fuse-ld` option. In this way, you want to set `-fuse-ld=lld` to
LDFLAGS when building your programs.

LLD leaves its name and version number to a `.comment` section in an
output. If you are in doubt whether you are successfully using LLD or
not, run `readelf --string-dump .comment <output-file>` and examine the
output. If the string "Linker: LLD" is included in the output, you are
using LLD.

## Internals

For the internals of the linker, please read {doc}`NewLLD`. It is a bit
outdated but the fundamental concepts remain valid. We'll update the
document soon.

```{toctree}
:maxdepth: 1

WebAssembly

ReleaseNotes

ELF/linker_script
ELF/start-stop-gc
ELF/warn_backrefs
MachO/index

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20.0)
if("${CMAKE_VERSION}" VERSION_LESS "3.31.0")
  message(WARNING
    "Your CMake version is ${CMAKE_VERSION}. Starting with LLVM 24, the "
    "minimum version of CMake required to build LLVM will become 3.31.0, and "
    "using an older CMake will become an error. Please upgrade your CMake to "
    "at least 3.31.0 now to avoid issues in the future.")
endif()

set(LLVM_SUBPROJECT_TITLE "LLD")

if(NOT DEFINED LLVM_COMMON_CMAKE_UTILS)
  set(LLVM_COMMON_CMAKE_UTILS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../cmake)
endif()
include(${LLVM_COMMON_CMAKE_UTILS}/Modules/CMakePolicy.cmake
  NO_POLICY_SCOPE)

# If we are not building as a part of LLVM, build LLD as an
# standalone project, using LLVM as an external library:
if(CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR STREQUAL CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR)
  project(lld)
  set(LLD_BUILT_STANDALONE TRUE)
endif()

# Must go below project(..)
include(GNUInstallDirs)

if(LLD_BUILT_STANDALONE)
  set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17 CACHE STRING "C++ standard to conform to")
  set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED YES)
  set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS NO)

  set(CMAKE_INCLUDE_CURRENT_DIR ON)

  find_package(LLVM REQUIRED HINTS "${LLVM_CMAKE_DIR}")
  list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${LLVM_DIR}")

  # Turn into CACHE PATHs for overwriting
  set(LLVM_INCLUDE_DIRS ${LLVM_INCLUDE_DIRS} CACHE PATH "Path to llvm/include and any other header dirs needed")
  set(LLVM_BINARY_DIR "${LLVM_BINARY_DIR}" CACHE PATH "Path to LLVM build tree")
  set(LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../llvm" CACHE PATH "Path to LLVM source tree")

  find_program(LLVM_TABLEGEN_EXE "llvm-tblgen" ${LLVM_TOOLS_BINARY_DIR}
    NO_DEFAULT_PATH)

  # They are used as destination of target generators.
  set(LLVM_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_INTDIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${CMAKE_CFG_INTDIR}/bin)
  set(LLVM_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_INTDIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${CMAKE_CFG_INTDIR}/lib${LLVM_LIBDIR_SUFFIX})

  separate_arguments(LLVM_DEFINITIONS_LIST NATIVE_COMMAND ${LLVM_DEFINITIONS})
  add_definitions(${LLVM_DEFINITIONS_LIST})
  list(APPEND CMAKE_REQUIRED_DEFINITIONS ${LLVM_DEFINITIONS_LIST})

  include(AddLLVM)
  include(TableGen)
  include(HandleLLVMOptions)
  include(GetErrcMessages)
  include(CheckAtomic)

  set(PACKAGE_VERSION "${LLVM_PACKAGE_VERSION}")

  include_directories(${LLVM_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  link_directories(${LLVM_LIBRARY_DIRS})

  if(LLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS)
    find_package(Python3 ${LLVM_MINIMUM_PYTHON_VERSION} REQUIRED
      COMPONENTS Interpreter)

    # Check prebuilt llvm/utils.
    if(EXISTS ${LLVM_TOOLS_BINARY_DIR}/FileCheck${CMAKE_EXECUTABLE_SUFFIX}
        AND EXISTS ${LLVM_TOOLS_BINARY_DIR}/not${CMAKE_EXECUTABLE_SUFFIX})
      set(LLVM_UTILS_PROVIDED ON)
    endif()

    if(EXISTS ${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/lit/lit.py)
      # Note: path not really used, except for checking if lit was found
      set(LLVM_EXTERNAL_LIT ${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/lit/lit.py)
      if(EXISTS ${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/llvm-lit)
        add_subdirectory(${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/llvm-lit utils/llvm-lit)
      endif()
      if(NOT LLVM_UTILS_PROVIDED)
        add_subdirectory(${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/FileCheck utils/FileCheck)
        add_subdirectory(${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/not utils/not)
        set(LLVM_UTILS_PROVIDED ON)
        set(LLD_TEST_DEPS FileCheck not)
      endif()

      if (NOT TARGET llvm_gtest)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "llvm-gtest not found. Please install llvm-gtest or disable tests with -DLLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS=OFF")
      endif()
    else()
      # Seek installed Lit.
      find_program(LLVM_EXTERNAL_LIT
                   NAMES llvm-lit lit.py lit
                   PATHS "${LLVM_MAIN_SRC_DIR}/utils/lit"
                   DOC "Path to lit.py")
    endif()

    if(LLVM_EXTERNAL_LIT)
      # Define the default arguments to use with 'lit', and an option for the user
      # to override.
      set(LIT_ARGS_DEFAULT "-sv")
      if (MSVC OR XCODE)
        set(LIT_ARGS_DEFAULT "${LIT_ARGS_DEFAULT} --no-progress-bar")
      endif()
      set(LLVM_LIT_ARGS "${LIT_ARGS_DEFAULT}" CACHE STRING "Default options for lit")

      get_errc_messages(LLVM_LIT_ERRC_MESSAGES)

      # On Win32 hosts, provide an option to specify the path to the GnuWin32 tools.
      if(WIN32 AND NOT CYGWIN)
        set(LLVM_LIT_TOOLS_DIR "" CACHE PATH "Path to GnuWin32 tools")
      endif()
    else()
      set(LLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS OFF)
    endif()
  endif()
endif() # standalone

set(LLD_TOOLS_INSTALL_DIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}" CACHE PATH
    "Path for binary subdirectory (defaults to '${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}')")
mark_as_advanced(LLD_TOOLS_INSTALL_DIR)

set(LLD_SOURCE_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
set(LLD_INCLUDE_DIR ${LLD_SOURCE_DIR}/include )
set(LLD_BINARY_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR})

set(LLD_VENDOR ${PACKAGE_VENDOR} CACHE STRING
  "Vendor-specific text for showing with version information.")

if(LLD_VENDOR)
  add_definitions(-DLLD_VENDOR="${LLD_VENDOR}")
endif()

# Compute the LLD version from the LLVM version.
string(REGEX MATCH "[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?" LLD_VERSION
  ${PACKAGE_VERSION})
message(STATUS "LLD version: ${LLD_VERSION}")

string(REGEX REPLACE "([0-9]+)\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?" "\\1" LLD_VERSION_MAJOR
  ${LLD_VERSION})
string(REGEX REPLACE "[0-9]+\\.([0-9]+)(\\.[0-9]+)?" "\\1" LLD_VERSION_MINOR
  ${LLD_VERSION})

# Configure the Version.inc file.
configure_file(
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include/lld/Common/Version.inc.in
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/include/lld/Common/Version.inc)


if (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR STREQUAL CMAKE_BINARY_DIR)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "In-source builds are not allowed. CMake would overwrite "
"the makefiles distributed with LLVM. Please create a directory and run cmake "
"from there, passing the path to this source directory as the last argument. "
"This process created the file `CMakeCache.txt' and the directory "
"`CMakeFiles'. Please delete them.")
endif()

# Add path for custom modules.
list(INSERT CMAKE_MODULE_PATH 0
  "${LLD_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/modules"
  "${LLVM_COMMON_CMAKE_UTILS}/Modules"
  )

include(AddLLD)

option(LLD_USE_VTUNE
       "Enable VTune user task tracking."
       OFF)
if (LLD_USE_VTUNE)
  find_package(VTune)
  if (VTUNE_FOUND)
    include_directories(${VTune_INCLUDE_DIRS})
    list(APPEND LLVM_COMMON_LIBS ${VTune_LIBRARIES})
    add_definitions(-DLLD_HAS_VTUNE)
  endif()
endif()

option(LLD_BUILD_TOOLS
  "Build the lld tools. If OFF, just generate build targets." ON)

option(LLD_DEFAULT_LD_LLD_IS_MINGW
    "Use MinGW as the default backend for ld.lld. If OFF, ELF will be used." OFF)
if (LLD_DEFAULT_LD_LLD_IS_MINGW)
  add_definitions("-DLLD_DEFAULT_LD_LLD_IS_MINGW=1")
endif()

if (MSVC)
  add_definitions(-wd4530) # Suppress 'warning C4530: C++ exception handler used, but unwind semantics are not enabled.'
  add_definitions(-wd4062) # Suppress 'warning C4062: enumerator X in switch of enum Y is not handled' from system header.
endif()

include_directories(BEFORE
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/include
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include
  )

add_subdirectory(Common)
add_subdirectory(tools/lld)

if (LLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS)
  add_custom_target(LLDUnitTests)
  set_target_properties(LLDUnitTests PROPERTIES FOLDER "LLD/Tests")
  if (TARGET llvm_gtest)
    add_subdirectory(unittests)
  endif()
  add_subdirectory(test)
endif()

add_subdirectory(docs)
add_subdirectory(COFF)
add_subdirectory(ELF)
add_subdirectory(MachO)
add_subdirectory(MinGW)
add_subdirectory(wasm)

add_custom_target(lld-headers)
set_target_properties(lld-headers PROPERTIES FOLDER "Misc")
if (NOT LLVM_INSTALL_TOOLCHAIN_ONLY)
  install(DIRECTORY include/lld
    DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}"
    COMPONENT lld-headers
    FILES_MATCHING
    PATTERN "*.h"
    PATTERN "*.inc"
    )

  if (NOT LLVM_ENABLE_IDE)
    add_llvm_install_targets(install-lld-headers
                             DEPENDS lld-headers
                             COMPONENT lld-headers)
  endif()
endif()

# Custom target to install all lld libraries
add_custom_target(lld-libraries)
if (NOT LLVM_ENABLE_IDE)
  add_llvm_install_targets(install-lld-libraries
                           DEPENDS lld-libraries
                           COMPONENT lld-libraries)
endif()

get_property(LLD_LIBS GLOBAL PROPERTY LLD_ALL_LIBS)
if(LLD_LIBS)
  list(REMOVE_DUPLICATES LLD_LIBS)
  foreach(lib ${LLD_LIBS})
    add_dependencies(lld-libraries ${lib})
    if(NOT LLVM_ENABLE_IDE)
      add_dependencies(install-lld-libraries install-${lib})
      add_dependencies(install-lld-libraries-stripped install-${lib}-stripped)
    endif()
  endforeach()
endif()

add_subdirectory(cmake/modules)

content.content:
1	# 项目概览与定位
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	本讲是整本 LLD 学习手册的第一篇。读完本讲后，你应该能够：
6	
7	- 说清楚 **LLD 是什么**：它是 LLVM 项目中的高性能模块化链接器，用来替代各平台自带的系统链接器（GNU ld、MSVC link.exe、ld64 等）。
8	- 理解 LLD 在 **LLVM 工具链中的定位**，以及它最核心的几条特性：快、可作为库嵌入、始终是交叉链接器。
9	- 了解 LLD 同时支持的 **四种目标格式**（ELF / COFF / Mach-O / WebAssembly）以及它们对应的后端目录。
10	- 掌握阅读 LLD 源码时最该先读的两份文档 `docs/index.md` 与 `docs/NewLLD.md`，并从中提取出后续学习要用到的 **关键概念**（如 Symbol、SymbolTable、InputSection、Driver、Writer）。
11	
12	本讲不要求你懂 C++ 模板，也不要求你已经写过链接器。我们只读文档和顶层目录，目的是先建立一张「全局地图」，后面的讲义再带你逐层下钻。
13	
14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	在开始前，先用最朴素的语言把「链接器」这件事讲清楚。
17	
18	### 2.1 什么是编译，什么是链接
19	
20	当你写下一段 C 程序并执行 `clang hello.c -o hello` 时，背后其实发生了好几步：
21	
22	1. **预处理**：展开 `#include`、`#define`。
23	2. **编译**：把每个 `.c` 源文件翻译成一个 **目标文件**（object file，Unix 下扩展名通常是 `.o`，Windows 下是 `.obj`）。
24	3. **链接**：把若干个目标文件、静态库（`.a` / `.lib`）、动态库（`.so` / `.dll`）**拼装成一个可执行文件或共享库**。
25	
26	第 3 步就是 **链接器（linker）** 干的活。你可以把它理解成一个「组装车间」：
27	
28	- 它读入一堆零件（目标文件、库）；
29	- 它把每个零件里用到的「符号」（函数名、全局变量名）**对上号**，决定谁定义了谁、谁引用了谁；
30	- 它把所有零件按规则排列到输出文件里，分配地址；
31	- 它把每处「这里要调用函数 foo」的占位改写成 foo 的真实地址（这一步叫 **重定位 relocation**）；
32	- 最后把结果写到磁盘上。
33	
34	### 2.2 什么是「目标格式」
35	
36	目标文件、可执行文件、共享库，本质上都是按某种 **二进制布局规范** 组织的字节流，这种规范就叫 **目标格式（object file format）**。不同操作系统用不同的格式：
37	
38	| 操作系统 | 主要目标格式 | 传统系统链接器 |
39	| --- | --- | --- |
40	| Linux / 各种 Unix | ELF | GNU ld / gold |
41	| Windows | PE / COFF | MSVC `link.exe` |
42	| macOS | Mach-O | `ld64` |
43	| （跨平台） | WebAssembly（wasm） | — |
44	
45	LLD 的特别之处在于：**同一个可执行文件就能处理上面这四种格式**。这是本讲后面要重点讲的事。
46	
47	### 2.3 阅读本讲你只需要
48	
49	- 一台装了 `clang` / `gcc` 和 `readelf` 的 Linux 环境（用于可选的动手实验）。
50	- 会用命令行、能看懂简单的英文文档。
51	- 知道「函数」「全局变量」这种基础编程概念。
52	
53	> 本讲引用的所有源码都是真实文件，行号与永久链接均对应当前 HEAD `8bdbeac21ecc`。
54	
55	## 3. 本讲源码地图
56	
57	本讲主要读文档与顶层目录，涉及的「源码」其实是项目自身的说明文件：
58	
59	| 文件 / 目录 | 作用 |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| `README.md` | LLD 仓库的最顶层说明，告诉你这是什么、许可证、基准测试数据出处。 |
62	| `docs/index.md` | LLD 的「门面文档」：定位、特性清单、性能对比、构建与使用方法。是初学者最该先读的一篇。 |
63	| `docs/NewLLD.md` | LLD 的 **设计与内部原理** 文档。官方说它「有点过时但核心概念仍然有效」，是阅读源码前必须建立的概念地图。 |
64	| 顶层目录（`ELF/`、`COFF/`、`MachO/`、`wasm/`、`MinGW/`、`Common/`、`include/`、`tools/`、`test/`、`unittests/`） | 用于直观感受「一个二进制、四个后端」的目录组织。本讲只看目录名，深入留到 u1-l3。 |
65	
66	记住一个总线索：**`docs/index.md` 回答「LLD 是什么、怎么用」，`docs/NewLLD.md` 回答「LLD 内部是怎么设计的」**。本讲的三个最小模块正是围绕这两份文档展开。
67	
68	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
69	
70	本讲拆成三个最小模块：
71	
72	- **4.1 LLD 项目定位与特性** —— 它是什么、为什么存在。
73	- **4.2 支持的目标格式与后端** —— 一个二进制怎么处理四种格式。
74	- **4.3 NewLLD 设计文档的关键概念** —— 读源码前要先记住的那张「概念地图」。
75	
76	---
77	
78	### 4.1 LLD 项目定位与特性
79	
80	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
81	
82	LLD 的全称是 **LLVM Linker**。它是 LLVM 编译器基础设施项目的一个子项目，定位非常明确：**做一个能直接替换各平台系统链接器、而且跑得快得多的链接器**。
83	
84	> 所谓「drop-in replacement（直接替换）」，是指它尽量接受和原系统链接器 **一样的命令行参数、一样的链接脚本**，这样你不用改构建脚本，只要换个链接器就能用上。
85	
86	最顶层 `README.md` 第一句话就把这层关系点明了：
87	
88	> 「This directory and its subdirectories contain source code for the LLVM Linker, a modular cross platform linker which is built as part of the LLVM compiler infrastructure project.」
89	> —— 这句话的关键词是 **modular（模块化）** 和 **cross platform（跨平台）**。
90	
91	参考：[README.md:1-9](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/README.md#L1-L9)
92	
93	#### 4.1.2 核心流程：LLD 在工具链里的位置
94	
95	用一个流程图式文字来表示 clang + LLD 的工作流：
96	
97	```
98	源文件 (.c/.cpp)
99	   │  clang -c 编译
100	   ▼
101	目标文件 (.o)  ──┐
102	静态库 (.a)    ──┤   clang -fuse-ld=lld
103	共享库 (.so)   ──┼────────────────────►  LLD (ld.lld)  ──►  可执行文件 / 共享库
104	LLVM bitcode  ──┘                        （链接）
105	```
106	
107	注意：在 Unix 上，链接器 **几乎从不被直接调用**，而是由编译器驱动（clang / gcc）在背后代为调用。你只要告诉 clang「请用 lld 来链接」（通过 `-fuse-ld=lld`），clang 就会把合适的参数传给 `ld.lld`。
108	
109	#### 4.1.3 源码精读：特性清单
110	
111	LLD 自我宣称的特性都在 `docs/index.md` 的 Features 小节。我们逐条对照真实文档来读。
112	
113	定位总纲（开头三句）：
114	
115	[docs/index.md:1-6](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L1-L6) —— 中文要点：LLD 是 LLVM 项目出品的链接器，是系统链接器的 **drop-in replacement（直接替换品）**，速度快得多，并且为工具链开发者提供了有用的特性。
116	
117	完整的特性清单在 Features 小节，整理成下表（每条都来自原文）：
118	
119	[docs/index.md:13-48](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L13-L48)
120	
121	| 特性 | 原文要点 | 给初学者的解释 |
122	| --- | --- | --- |
123	| **直接替换 GNU ld** | accepts the same command line arguments and linker scripts as GNU | 不用改构建脚本就能换上。 |
124	| **非常快** | more than twice as fast as the GNU gold linker | 多核机器上常比 gold 快两倍以上。 |
125	| **支持众多 CPU/ABI** | AArch64, AMDGPU, ARM, Hexagon, LoongArch, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V, SPARC V9, x86-32/64 | 一个链接器管一大片架构。 |
126	| **始终是交叉链接器** | always a cross-linker ... no build-time option to enable/disable each target | 不管你怎么编译 LLD，它都支持全部目标；天然适合交叉编译。 |
127	| **可作为库嵌入** | embed LLD in your program ... call `lld::lldMain` | 不必起子进程，直接在程序里调用链接。 |
128	| **代码体积小** | 21k lines of C++ (2017 数据) vs gold 198k | 没有抽象层，所以又快又好读。 |
129	| **默认支持 LTO** | Link-time optimization is supported by default | 传 `-flto` 给 clang 即可全程序优化。 |
130	| **为 21 世纪调过默认值** | stack marked non-executable by default | 默认栈不可执行，安全性更高。 |
131	
132	这八条就是 LLD 的「卖点清单」。其中**快、可作为库、始终是交叉链接器**这三条，是后续讲义会反复出现的设计动机，建议重点记住。
133	
134	#### 4.1.4 代码实践：从文档反查「怎么确认我用的是 LLD」
135	
136	这是一道「源码阅读 + 命令验证」型练习。
137	
138	1. **实践目标**：搞清楚「如何确认一个输出文件确实是由 LLD 链接出来的」。
139	2. **操作步骤**：
140	   - 打开 [docs/index.md:107-111](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L107-L111)（「Using LLD」小节末尾）。
141	   - 文档明确写：LLD 会把自己的名字和版本写进输出文件的 `.comment` 段；如果输出里包含字符串 `Linker: LLD`，就说明用了 LLD。
142	3. **要观察的现象**：在本地执行（待本地验证）
143	
144	   ```bash
145	   clang hello.c -fuse-ld=lld -o hello
146	   readelf --string-dump .comment hello
147	   ```
148	
149	4. **预期结果**：`readelf` 的输出里能看到形如 `Linker: LLD x.y.z` 的字符串。
150	5. 如果你本地没装 `ld.lld`，那么「阅读文档得出结论」本身就已经完成了这道练习——你已经从源文档里找到了答案。
151	
152	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
153	
154	**练习 1**：`docs/index.md` 说 LLD 是「drop-in replacement for the GNU linkers」，这句话对使用者意味着什么？
155	
156	> **参考答案**：意味着 LLD 尽量复用 GNU ld 的命令行参数和链接脚本语法，使用者无需修改现有的 `Makefile` / `CMakeLists.txt` / 链接脚本，只要把链接器换成 `ld.lld`（例如给 clang 加 `-fuse-ld=lld`）就能直接工作。
157	
158	**练习 2**：为什么 LLD 强调「stack 默认不可执行」是一种安全改进？
159	
160	> **参考答案**：可执行栈会让攻击者更容易利用栈溢出漏洞（把恶意代码塞进栈里并跳过去执行）。默认把栈标记为不可执行（NX），等于关掉了一条常见的攻击路径。LLD 把它设为默认值，是为现代安全要求调优的体现。
161	
162	---
163	
164	### 4.2 支持的目标格式与后端
165	
166	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
167	
168	绝大多数链接器只服务于一种格式：GNU ld 只懂 ELF，MSVC link 只懂 COFF，ld64 只懂 Mach-O。**LLD 的独特之处是同一个二进制里同时塞了四个链接器**，分别处理四种格式：
169	
170	- **ELF**（Unix，Linux 主力）
171	- **PE/COFF**（Windows）
172	- **Mach-O**（macOS）
173	- **WebAssembly**
174	
175	`docs/index.md` 在开头就给出了这四种格式，并按「成熟度」排了序：
176	
177	> 「The linker supports ELF (Unix), PE/COFF (Windows), Mach-O (macOS) and WebAssembly in descending order of completeness. Internally, LLD consists of several different linkers.」
178	
179	参考：[docs/index.md:7-11](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L7-L11)
180	
181	注意「Internally, LLD consists of several different linkers」这句——这是理解整个项目结构的钥匙：**它不是一个能处理多种格式的链接器，而是四个链接器共用一个外壳**。
182	
183	#### 4.2.2 核心流程：四种格式 ↔ 四个目录
184	
185	这一点直接体现在仓库的顶层目录上。下表把「目标格式」和「源码目录」「对应的可执行文件名」对应起来：
186	
187	| 目标格式 | 源码目录 | 传统调用名（LLD 的符号链接名） |
188	| --- | --- | --- |
189	| ELF | `ELF/` | `ld.lld` |
190	| PE/COFF | `COFF/` | `lld-link` |
191	| Mach-O | `MachO/` | `ld64.lld` |
192	| WebAssembly | `wasm/` | `wasm-ld` |
193	| （特殊）GNU 风格的 Windows 交叉编译 | `MinGW/` | （薄包装，转交给 COFF 后端） |
194	| 公共基础设施 | `Common/`、`include/lld/Common/` | （被四个后端共享） |
195	| 单一可执行文件入口 / 分发器 | `tools/lld/` | `lld`（根据调用名分发） |
196	
197	> 「四个后端 + 一个公共层 + 一个分发器」就是 LLD 源码组织的全貌。深入到每个目录内部、看它们各自有哪些共性模块（Driver / SymbolTable / Writer / ...），是 u1-l3 的任务，这里只要记住这张总表。
198	
199	关于 ELF 后端支持的 CPU/ABI 范围，文档列得很细，值得原样记下（生产级与可用的区分对未来排错很有用）：
200	
201	[docs/index.md:20-24](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L20-L24) —— 列出 AArch64、AMDGPU、ARM、Hexagon、LoongArch、MIPS 32/64（大/小端）、PowerPC、PowerPC64、RISC-V、SPARC V9、x86-32、x86-64，并标注其中 AArch64、ARM(≥v4)、LoongArch、PowerPC、PowerPC64、RISC-V、x86-32、x86-64 为生产级，MIPS「看起来也不错」。
202	
203	#### 4.2.3 源码精读：为什么是「共享设计但不共享代码」
204	
205	这是 `NewLLD.md` 第一条设计决策，必须读懂，否则你会困惑「为什么 ELF 和 COFF 里有那么多名字一样的类却不复用」。
206	
207	[docs/NewLLD.md:28-37](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L28-L37) —— 原文要点：
208	
209	- 把每种格式都实现成 **native linker（原生链接器）**；
210	- 它们 **共享设计思想（share the same design），但几乎不共享代码（share very little code）**；
211	- 原因：各种目标格式差别大到「为了抽象它们而加的中间层」并不划算，反而增加复杂度和运行时开销；去掉抽象层大大简化了实现。
212	
213	用一句话总结这张图：
214	
215	```
216	   设计哲学（Driver / SymbolTable / Writer / InputFile ...）  ← 共享
217	        │                │                │             │
218	       ELF             COFF            MachO          wasm      ← 各自独立实现
219	   (InputSection)    (Chunk)          ...           ...        ← 数据结构都不同
220	```
221	
222	正因为如此，本手册 **以 ELF 为主线** 讲解（第二单元起），再在第八单元横向对比 COFF / Mach-O / wasm。
223	
224	#### 4.2.4 代码实践：手工绘制「格式—目录—调用名」对照表
225	
226	这是一道纯目录阅读型练习，不需要编译。
227	
228	1. **实践目标**：凭观察仓库结构，验证「一个二进制四个后端」的说法。
229	2. **操作步骤**：
230	   - 在仓库根目录查看有哪些后端目录（`ELF/ COFF/ MachO/ wasm/ MinGW/`）。
231	   - 查阅 `docs/index.md` 的「Using LLD」小节 [docs/index.md:91-106](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L91-L106)，确认 LLD 安装后的可执行名是 `ld.lld`，并理解它由编译器驱动代为调用。
232	3. **要观察的现象**：每个格式都对应一个独立目录；公共代码集中在 `Common/` 与 `include/`。
233	4. **预期结果**：你能不看本讲，自己默写出 4.2.2 节那张表。
234	
235	#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案
236	
237	**练习 1**：如果有人问「为什么 LLD 里 `ELF/InputSection.h` 和 `COFF/Chunks.h` 干的是类似的活，却不抽一个公共基类」，你怎么用 NewLLD.md 的话回答？
238	
239	> **参考答案**：因为各目标格式差异巨大，抽象公共层「得不偿失」——抽象层带来的复杂度与运行时开销，超过了代码复用的收益。所以 LLD 选择让每个后端各写一套原生实现，共享的是设计思想而非代码。（依据 [docs/NewLLD.md:28-37](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L28-L37)）
240	
241	**练习 2**：文档说四种格式是「in descending order of completeness」，请说出排序。
242	
243	> **参考答案**：ELF（最完整）> PE/COFF > Mach-O > WebAssembly。其中 COFF 端「完整，包括 Windows 调试信息（PDB）支持」。（依据 [docs/index.md:7-11](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L7-L11)）
244	
245	---
246	
247	### 4.3 NewLLD 设计文档的关键概念
248	
249	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
250	
251	`docs/NewLLD.md` 是阅读 LLD 源码前 **必须先读** 的文档。它在开头就说明了我们为什么要在第 1 讲就读它——作者把链接器拆解成少数几个 **关键数据结构（Important Data Structures）** 和 **三个主要角色（three actors）**，并说：
252	
253	> 「the linker can be understood as the interactions between them. Once you understand their functions, the code of the linker should look obvious to you.」
254	
255	参考：[docs/NewLLD.md:133-138](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L133-L138)
256	
257	换句话说，**只要记住这几个概念，后面读源码就不会迷路**。这就是本模块要建立的那张「概念地图」。
258	
259	#### 4.3.2 核心流程：三条设计原则 + 一组关键数据结构 + 三个角色
260	
261	把 NewLLD.md 的设计部分归纳成一张总图：
262	
263	```
264	┌──────────────── 三条高层设计原则（Key Concepts）────────────────┐
265	│  1. Native linkers：原生实现，共享设计不共享代码              │
266	│  2. Speed by design：少做事 > 高效地做事（惰性求值）          │
267	│  3. Efficient archive handling：记住全部符号，按需即时提取   │
268	└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
269	         │ 指导着下面这些数据结构与角色的实现
270	         ▼
271	┌───── 关键数据结构（Important Data Structures）─────┐
272	│  Symbol(Defined/Undefined/Lazy)                   │
273	│  SymbolTable   (字符串 → Symbol 的哈希表 + 冲突解决)│
274	│  InputSection (ELF) / Chunk (COFF)                │
275	│  OutputSection (InputSection/Chunk 的容器)         │
276	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
277	         │ 被下面三个角色驱动
278	         ▼
279	┌────────────── 三个角色（three actors）──────────────┐
280	│  InputFile ：读入文件，创建并持有 Symbol / Section  │
281	│  Driver    ：解析命令行、建符号表、串联整个流程     │
282	│  Writer    ：分配地址、把结果写到输出文件           │
283	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
284	```
285	
286	下面把每个概念对照原文讲清楚。
287	
288	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
289	
290	**（a）三条设计原则**
291	
292	[docs/NewLLD.md:19-102](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L19-L102)
293	
294	1. **Speed by design（靠设计来提速）**：原文最经典的一句是「do less rather than do it efficiently」（少做事，胜过把事做得更高效）。具体表现为 **惰性求值**——「不到必须时不读 section 内容和重定位」；对每个符号只查一次哈希表，之后直接用指针这种「handle」。这条原则解释了为什么 LLD 源码里到处是「先记下指针、后面再用」的写法。
295	
296	2. **Efficient archive handling（高效的归档/静态库处理）**：传统 Unix 链接器只记住「未定义符号集合」，按命令行顺序扫描，遇到归档就从中抽出能解决这些未定义符号的成员；这导致「库放在目标文件之前就什么都不抽」、以及「互相依赖的库需要 `--start-group/--end-group` 反复扫描」的问题。LLD 的做法是 **记住所有符号**，一旦发现某个未定义符号能由之前见过的归档成员解决，就 **立刻** 抽取并链接。因此 `--start-group/--end-group` 在 LLD 里基本是 no-op（u4-l4 会深入）。
297	
298	**（b）需要记住的「量级」**
299	
300	[docs/NewLLD.md:104-131](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L104-L131) —— 链接一个约 2 GB 的 Chrome（带调试信息）时，LLD 要读：
301	
302	- 17,000 个文件
303	- 1,800,000 个段（section）
304	- 6,300,000 个符号（symbol）
305	- 13,000,000 个重定位（relocation）
306	
307	最终 **15 秒** 产出 2 GB 可执行文件。
308	
309	文档还给了关于性能直觉的关键提醒：符号字符串总量 450 MB，全部插入哈希表要 1.5 秒；因此「给每个符号随手多加一次哈希查询，就会让链接器慢 10%」。这解释了为什么 LLD 对符号操作极其抠细节，却对「文件数量」不那么在意。
310	
311	**（c）关键数据结构**
312	
313	[docs/NewLLD.md:139-204](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L139-L204) 整理如下：
314	
315	| 概念 | 中文要点 | 后续在哪深入 |
316	| --- | --- | --- |
317	| **Symbol** | 每个唯一符号名只有 **一个** Symbol 实例；分 Defined / Undefined / Lazy 三类；用 **placement new** 就地替换，使旧指针自动指向解析结果。 | u4-l1 |
318	| **SymbolTable** | 字符串 → Symbol 的哈希表，外加 **按符号类型解决冲突** 的逻辑（Defined vs Undefined vs Lazy）。 | u4-l2 |
319	| **Chunk**（仅 COFF） | COFF 里表示「输出中的一块数据」，知道自己的大小、如何拷贝到 mmap 输出、如何应用重定位。对应 ELF 的 InputSection。 | u8-l1 |
320	| **InputSection**（仅 ELF） | ELF 直接把输入节当作内部数据类型，职责与 COFF Chunk 类似。 | u5-l1 |
321	| **OutputSection** | InputSection / Chunk 的 **容器**；每个 InputSection/Chunk 至多属于一个 OutputSection。 | u5-l1 |
322	
323	**（d）三个角色**
324	
325	[docs/NewLLD.md:205-231](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L205-L231) —— Driver 是总指挥，它的职责原文写得非常清楚：
326	
327	1. 处理命令行选项；
328	2. 创建符号表；
329	3. 为每个输入文件创建 InputFile，把符号放进符号表；
330	4. 检查是否还有未解析的未定义符号；
331	5. 创建 Writer；
332	6. 把符号表交给 Writer，写出结果。
333	
334	这六步，几乎就是后续讲义第二单元 ELF 主线的提纲。
335	
336	> 小提示：NewLLD.md 里把 LTO 也点了一下——「把 LLVM bitcode 当作普通目标文件来解析符号，全部解析成功后再用 LLVM 把所有 bitcode 编译成一个大对象，最后把 bitcode 符号替换成 ELF/COFF 符号」。详见 [docs/NewLLD.md:233-243](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L233-L243)，深入留到 u7-l3。
337	
338	#### 4.3.4 代码实践：把 NewLLD.md 浓缩成「概念卡片」
339	
340	这是一道阅读理解 + 整理型练习，目的是让你把文档真正「吃进去」。
341	
342	1. **实践目标**：用自己的话，把 NewLLD.md 的设计部分浓缩成不超过 10 行的笔记。
343	2. **操作步骤**：
344	   - 通读 [docs/NewLLD.md:15-231](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L15-L231)。
345	   - 用三个小标题分别写出：「三条设计原则」「四个关键数据结构」「三个角色及其职责」。
346	3. **要观察的现象**：你会发现后续每一篇讲义的标题，几乎都能在这张笔记里找到对应。
347	4. **预期结果**：得到一张类似 4.3.2 节总图的个人笔记。如果你写不出某一条，就回去重读对应行号。
348	
349	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
350	
351	**练习 1**：用 NewLLD.md 里「placement new 就地替换 Symbol」的机制，解释「为什么指向某个未定义符号的指针，在符号被解析成已定义符号后会自动指向新结果」。
352	
353	> **参考答案**：因为符号表保证「每个唯一的符号名只对应一个 Symbol 实例」，解析时不是新建对象再改指针，而是用 placement new 在 **同一块内存上** 用更好的 Symbol 覆盖旧对象。所以原本指向那块内存的指针，读出来的自然是新的（已定义）符号。（依据 [docs/NewLLD.md:155-166](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L155-L166)）
354	
355	**练习 2**：为什么 NewLLD.md 说「不要给每个符号随手加一次哈希查询」？
356	
357	> **参考答案**：因为符号数量巨大（量级在百万级），符号字符串总量可达数百 MB，把它们全部插入哈希表本身就要秒级。每多一次「随手」的哈希查询，就会显著拖慢整个链接器（原文举例：慢 10%）。所以 LLD 强调对每个符号只查一次、之后用指针作为 handle。（依据 [docs/NewLLD.md:124-128](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L124-L128)）
358	
359	**练习 3**：列出 Driver 的六项职责（按顺序）。
360	
361	> **参考答案**：①处理命令行选项 → ②创建符号表 → ③为每个输入文件创建 InputFile 并把符号放入符号表 → ④检查没有遗留的未定义符号 → ⑤创建 Writer → ⑥把符号表交给 Writer 写出结果。（依据 [docs/NewLLD.md:222-231](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L222-L231)）
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 5. 综合实践
366	
367	本讲的综合实践把「定位 / 特性 / 文档」三件事串起来：**亲手用 LLD 链接一个程序，并从输出和文档里双向验证 LLD 的特性**。
368	
369	**实践目标**
370	
371	- 用 `clang -fuse-ld=lld` 链接一个 hello world；
372	- 用 `readelf` 从输出文件中证明它确实由 LLD 产生；
373	- 对照 `docs/index.md`，列出 LLD 相对 GNU ld 的三条核心优势。
374	
375	**操作步骤**
376	
377	1. 准备一个最简单的 C 程序 `hello.c`：
378	
379	   ```c
380	   #include <stdio.h>
381	   int main(void) { printf("hello, lld\n"); return 0; }
382	   ```
383	
384	2. 用 LLD 链接（需要本地已安装 `ld.lld`；待本地验证）：
385	
386	   ```bash
387	   clang hello.c -fuse-ld=lld -o hello
388	   ```
389	
390	3. 检查 `.comment` 段，确认链接器身份：
391	
392	   ```bash
393	   readelf --string-dump .comment hello
394	   ```
395	
396	4. 对照 [docs/index.md:13-48](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L13-L48)，挑出你认为最重要的「相对 GNU ld 的三条优势」，并各用一句话写出依据。
397	
398	**需要观察的现象**
399	
400	- 步骤 2 能成功生成可执行文件 `hello`，运行 `./hello` 输出 `hello, lld`。
401	- 步骤 3 的输出中包含 `Linker: LLD ...` 字样（这是文档 [docs/index.md:107-111](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L107-L111) 明确承诺的标记）。
402	
403	**预期结果**
404	
405	- 二进制确实由 LLD 链接（`.comment` 段含 `Linker: LLD`）。
406	- 三条优势的参考答案（你的表述可以不同）：
407	  1. **快**：多核上常比 GNU gold 还快两倍以上（[docs/index.md:17-19](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L17-L19) 与性能表 [docs/index.md:56-63](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L56-L63)）。
408	  2. **可作为库嵌入**：直接在程序里调用 `lld::lldMain`，免去外部链接器依赖（[docs/index.md:29-33](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L29-L33)）。
409	  3. **始终是交叉链接器**：不管怎么编译都支持全部目标架构，适合交叉编译工具链（[docs/index.md:25-28](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L25-L28)）。
410	
411	> 如果你本地没有 `ld.lld`，无法执行步骤 2/3，请把本实践降级为「文档阅读型」：直接从 `docs/index.md` 与 `docs/NewLLD.md` 中找出上述答案并写下来即可——这同样达成本讲的学习目标。
412	
413	**附：性能对比的直观感受**
414	
415	`docs/index.md` 给出的性能表里，以 `clang dbg`（1.67 GiB 输出）为例：GNU ld 用时 104.03s，而 `lld w/threads` 仅 5.28s。加速比约为
416	
417	\[
418	\text{加速比} = \frac{104.03}{5.28} \approx 19.7\times
419	\]
420	
421	再用 `chromium dbg`（1.14 GiB）算一次：
422	
423	\[
424	\text{加速比} = \frac{209.05}{16.70} \approx 12.5\times
425	\]
426	
427	可见在大程序上 LLD 相对 GNU ld 快了一个数量级，这正是「LLD 很快」这条特性最直观的证据（数据来源 [docs/index.md:56-63](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L56-L63)）。
428	
429	## 6. 本讲小结
430	
431	- **LLD 是 LLVM 项目的高性能模块化链接器**，目标是直接替换各平台的系统链接器（[README.md:1-9](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/README.md#L1-L9)）。
432	- 它最核心的三条特性是 **快、可作为库嵌入、始终是交叉链接器**（[docs/index.md:13-48](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L13-L48)）。
433	- **同一个二进制里装了四个链接器**，分别处理 ELF / COFF / Mach-O / WebAssembly，对应 `ELF/ COFF/ MachO/ wasm/` 四个目录（[docs/index.md:7-11](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L7-L11)）。
434	- 四个后端 **共享设计、几乎不共享代码**，没有抽象公共层（[docs/NewLLD.md:28-37](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L28-L37)）。
435	- 阅读源码前要先把 `docs/NewLLD.md` 的「关键数据结构（Symbol / SymbolTable / InputSection·Chunk / OutputSection）」与「三个角色（InputFile / Driver / Writer）」记牢（[docs/NewLLD.md:133-231](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/NewLLD.md#L133-L231)）。
436	- 想确认输出是否由 LLD 链接，看 `.comment` 段里有没有 `Linker: LLD`（[docs/index.md:107-111](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/8bdbeac21eccd679489614e0326ab398425d47f1/lld/docs/index.md#L107-L111)）。
437	
438	## 7. 下一步学习建议
439	
440	本讲只建立了「LLD 是什么」的全局印象，还没有真正碰 C++ 源码。建议按下面的顺序继续：
441	
442	1. **先补齐工程基础**：阅读 u1-l2《构建与运行 LLD》，亲手用 CMake 把 `ld.lld` 编出来；再读 u1-l3《目录结构与多后端源码组织》，把 4.2.2 节那张总表细化到「每个后端目录里都有哪些共性文件」。
443	2. **再读分发机制**：阅读 u1-l4《单一可执行文件与 flavor 分发机制》，理解 `tools/lld/lld.cpp` 怎么根据调用名把控制权交给四个后端之一。这一篇会把你本讲看到的「一个二进制四个后端」彻底落到代码上。
444	3. **配合官方文档**：继续精读 `docs/NewLLD.md` 的后半部分（Important Data Structures 之后），并把它和 u2「ELF 链接主线」对照——你会发现第二单元讲的 `link<ELFT>` 流水线，正是本讲 4.3.2 节那张「Driver 六步」的展开版。
445
